text:
maria: Heads up — Acme support ticket #7893: customers seeing repeated 5xxs and p95 timeouts on hosted inference around 14:40 UTC. Symptoms: long tail latencies, some requests 504/502. Any quick triage?

jane-cs: Customer provided sample request_id `req_0a1b2c`. Logs show a lot of queued requests and some rapid retries. They say latency spikes coincide with a bulk job run.

suresh: Looking at runtime metrics — continuous-batcher backlog shooting up, queue depth hitting the configured hard limit (route.queue_depth=800). Dequeue throughput collapsed; lots of workers blocked on a handful of long-sequence requests (>= 64k tokens). Head-of-line blocking.

tom: Confirm — scheduler traces show multiple batchers pinned waiting for an in-flight long-seq from tenant `acme-runner`. While that's executing, small requests pile up and hit tail-timeouts. Also saw transient 5xx when the fallback model was invoked and failed due to resource starvation.

maria: Can we repro locally to validate mitigation? What's the repro sequence?

suresh: Yes repro is straightforward — stream a few long-context requests simultaneously to the hosted route and then fire a bunch of short requests to observe tail-timeouts. Example repro (be careful, this will consume GPU):

```bash
# simulate long in-flight requests (adjust URL/API_KEY)
for i in {1..3}; do \ 
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/hosted/infer \ 
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_KEY" \ 
    -H "X-Tenant: acme-runner" \ 
    -d '{"model":"rwlm-large","input":"'$(python -c 'print("x"*65000)')'","stream":false}' &
done
# then hammer with short requests
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/hosted/infer -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY" -d '{"model":"rwlm-small","input":"hi"}' & done
wait
```

jane-cs: Customer also noted an auth hiccup earlier — token rotated but retries looked healthy afterward. Billing shows spike in token consumption during the incident window.

suresh: Root cause summary: continuous batching packs the long requests and they dominate GPU time. That increases effective per-request latency, queue depth climbs, and shorter requests start hitting tail timeouts or receive 5xx during model fallback. Secondary factor: route-level queue_depth and batch_window settings tuned for throughput (larger batch windows) exacerbate head-of-line.

tom: Immediate mitigation steps I recommend and executed:
1) For tenant `acme-runner` set a per-tenant concurrency cap and short-circuit very-long-seq requests (reject or route to dedicated pool).
2) Temporarily lower continuous-batcher `batch_window_ms` from 200ms -> 50ms on hosted-llm-3 cluster to reduce packing of long jobs.
3) Enable emergency autoscale and add an inbound short-request priority queue.

Admin command I ran (internal admin API):
```json
PATCH /internal/tenants/acme-runner/config
{ "max_concurrent_requests": 10, "reject_long_sequences_above_tokens": 20000 }
```

```bash
# reduce batch window via admin CLI
redwood admin routing update --cluster hosted-llm-3 --route default --set batch_window_ms=50
```

maria: Thanks. Any quick observations on whether the fallback 5xxs were due to model swap failures vs gateway saturation?

suresh: Mostly gateway saturation. The model process occasionally OOMed when under extreme packing, which triggered a cascade: worker crashed -> requests retried -> queue depth + retries -> more pressure. So a small number of model failures amplified the backlog.

maria: Action items (tracked):
- suresh: add prefilter that rejects >20k token requests from hosted public pool and returns 429 with descriptive message.
- tom: keep emergency autoscale and monitor p95, queue_depth, batcher.backlog.
- jane-cs: communicate mitigation to the customer and ask for their job cadence to help root cause.
- follow-up: evaluate queue_depth default and add head-of-line detection alert.

tom: Pushed quick changes: lowered batch_window and adjusted autoscale. Deploy bot says: 

deploy-bot: deploy hosted-llm-3 batch-window-change succeeded (commit 3a9f1b2) :white_check_mark:

jane-cs: Customer accepted throttling and will reschedule the bulk job to their dedicated pool. They are monitoring; asked us to keep them posted for 2 hours.

maria: Closing interim support loop — we'll file full postmortem if metrics don't stabilize. Great job triaging quickly. :thumbsup:

jane-cs: Closing ticket if stable in 2h, will reopen with artifacts otherwise.
